findings.title: D9 mitigation skips the `gemini` profile, the one most likely to report false substitutions
findings.description:
Plan Part C (slice plan line 443) says design "must decide what counts as 'differs' for providers that return a dated or routed variant of the requested id … so an alias resolving to its own snapshot is not reported as a substitution."

D9 chooses an exact rule and relies on Phase 6 to catch false positives: it will capture "one review per configured profile (sdk, openai, openrouter, local)". The same four profiles appear in Verification Walkthrough step 6 (lines 348–353) and in the Mitigation Strategies (line 363). `gemini` is missing from all three, but it is a registered profile (`ProviderType.GEMINI`, with `[aliases.gemini]` in `data/models.toml`). Slice 906 also lists it in the six-profile matrix.

Gemini is the profile most likely to break the exact rule. Its default aliases use preview and variant ids such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools` and `gemini-3-flash-preview`. If its OpenAI-compatible endpoint reports a shortened, prefixed or base form of the id, every gemini review will write `requestedModel:` and log a WARNING. It would also take on a new metrology judge identity. That is the risk the design names at line 359, on a profile it never checks.

Fix: add `gemini` to the D9 capture list, walkthrough step 6, and the mitigation. Better, derive the list from the registered profiles rather than writing it out by hand, so a new profile can't be skipped again.

findings.title: "Not reported" doesn't separate Codex from a stamping regression
findings.description:
D11 treats an empty `answering_models` the same way for every provider: a Run Digest line and no WARNING. For Codex that is right. For the SDK and OpenAI-compatible providers, D8 says they always report, so an empty list there means the stamping broke. The artifact would still state the gap, so this isn't a silent fallback. But the case is never logged and no test asserts it.

A cheap fix: log a WARNING only when a provider that is supposed to report returns nothing. Not required by the slice plan.

findings.title: Part B decision fits the plan and the verdict model
findings.description: The plan asked design to choose between forcing CONCERNS and failing the run. D4 chooses CONCERNS, gives its reasons, and keeps the "model did read files" carve-out the plan requires. D5 adds `VerdictSource.IMPOSED` and checks for consumers: no reader in context-forge, and slice 917's validator doesn't check `verdictSource`. D6 catches the side effect where a degraded parse would be hidden by the synthetic finding.

findings.title: Part A: frontmatter carries the minimum fact a gate needs, and the paths stay in parity
findings.description: The plan said "design picks the minimum that lets a gate decide." D1 and D2 put one boolean in frontmatter, using the same three states as `location_verified`. The counts go in the header and JSON. D3 adds the case where the diff was dropped entirely by the total-injection limit, which the plan missed. Both the CLI and pipeline paths go through `run_review_with_profile` and then `format_review_markdown`, so they produce the same keys.

findings.title: Scope, deferrals and size are proportionate
findings.description: Ordering the diff and adding `--stat` were allowed only "if design shows it is small", and D7 defers them to #137 with a reason. Each new module (`coverage.py`, `snapshot.py`) has one purpose and one consumer. The design keeps `review_client.py` (588 lines) from growing further and declines to extract injection code, which isn't this slice's job. The new mechanisms match an effort of 3/5.
